### DEV-123 — A12 (reversed `killed_by`) and A13 (citation resolvability) added; A11's comma-less-patronymic recall bug found and fixed; GAP-008's proposed detector built, measured at 82% noise, and recorded as a dead end

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | Post-P4, eighth and ninth of DEV-115's carried-forward items — DEV-121's lead (a) ("A11 has no non-parentage sibling") and GAP-008 (filed by DEV-122). Plus DEV-122's finding (4), the Telamon Pherecydes variant, taken as a follow-on. |
| **Original Plan** | DEV-121 lead (a): "a `killed_by` direction check is the obvious A11 companion." GAP-008: "for each seeded `parent_of` edge, check that the cited passage contains the child's name and the parent's name *inside one kinship construction*… A11's `_KINSHIP` regex is most of the machinery already." |
| **What Changed** | **A12 (`audit/kill_direction.py`, 12 tests) — built, and it earns its place: `killed_by` is 872 distinct candidate edges and no check had ever read one.** That gap was not theoretical — five of DEV-121's six direction fixes and both of DEV-122's were `killed_by`, and *every one was found by accident* while walking rows for another reason. Same evidentiary rule as A11 (`correct == 0`, alias-aware, reports only), both voices matched because Homer prefers the active ("Idomeneus slew Phaestus") and Frazer the passive ("Parthenopaeus was slain by Periclymenus"). **Two calibration findings, both kept as tests:** (1) the filler between the two names must **exclude capitalised words** — a third proper noun there is almost always the verb's real subject, and Iliad 15.47's "…Patroclus shall goodly Achilles slay Hector…" was being read as "Patroclus slew Hector", wrong twice over. Since every translation writes epithets in lower case, excluding capitals keeps the epithets and drops the intervening-subject case; the documented cost is that a patronymic in that position is no longer matched — lost recall, never a wrong report. (2) `(?-i:[a-z])` is load-bearing: the patterns compile with `re.IGNORECASE` so spellings match regardless of case, which silently made `[a-z]` match capitals and undid rule (1) entirely. A character-budget first cut (`[^.;:]{0,60}`) reported **16**; word budgets took it to 7; the case-scoping fix to **6**. **All 6 read against their passage: 5 genuine, 1 false positive.** **A13 (`audit/passage_support.py`, 7 tests) — GAP-008's proposed rule was built and it does not work.** Measured against the full corpus it flags **82% of 5,259 citations** (4,355). Two rounds of widening moved it 87% → 82% only, because the residue is structural, not lexical: **enumeration** (Apollodorus 3.12.5 lists ~40 sons of Priam after one verb — 252 characters from "Priam had sons" to "Echephron"), **relative clause** ("Helios whom mild-eyed Euryphaessa … bare to"), **coordination** ("Aeetes, son of the Sun…, and brother of Circe and Pasiphae" implies the parentage across two clauses), and **periphrasis** (Iliad 19's "the valiant son of Menoetius"). What shipped is the decidable part of the same scope: **a citation must resolve to a real segment.** Not trivial — `passage_ref` is the provenance the product shows a user, `seedgen` copies it through unchecked, and `relationships` has no review gate. **A11's own recall bug, found by A13's calibration run and fixed:** `_KINSHIP` began `(?:,\s*)?`, so nothing consumed the space in the **comma-less** patronymic and "Amphilochus son of Alcmaeon" — as common in Frazer and Murray as the comma'd form — scored **zero**; the possessive "Andraemon's son Thoas" was missed outright. Both fixed, with 3 regression tests. **The fix immediately surfaced a real reversed edge invisible to every prior run: `Echeclus parent_of Agenor`, against Iliad 20.474's "Agenor's son Echeclus".** **Telamon's Pherecydes variant promoted** (the follow-on): Apollodorus 3.12.6 states both traditions in one sentence — "Aeacus married Endeis … by whom he had two sons, Peleus and Telamon. **But Pherecydes says** that Telamon was a friend, not a brother of Peleus, he being a son of Actaeus and Glauce" — so `child of Aeacus`/`child of Endeis` and `child of Actaeus`/`child of Glauce` were promoted to `trust_tier=1`, the same shape DEV-119 promoted for Agamemnon/Plisthenes. |
| **Reason** | The user picked A12 and A13 off a ranked list, then added the Telamon promotion as a follow-on. A12 ranked first on measured evidence rather than symmetry: two consecutive passes had stumbled into reversed `killed_by` edges by accident, which is what an unchecked relation looks like from the outside. |

**A12's one known false-positive shape, waived rather than engineered around — pronoun anaphora.** Iliad 5.655 has both men strike: *"Sarpedon smote **him** full upon the neck, and the grievous point passed clean through, and down upon his eyes came the darkness of night"* (Tlepolemus dies — the seeded edge is **correct**), then *"And Tlepolemus smote Sarpedon upon the left thigh"* (a wound). A12 sees the second and not the first, because the kill names its victim with a pronoun. No regex over entity names resolves that reference, so `correct == 0` cannot suppress it. Waived with the passage quoted, and flagged in the README as the check's designed limit rather than a bug to fix later.

4. **A12 covers `killed_by` only.** `married_to` (344 seeded edges) and `sibling_of` (49) still have no direction or support check of any kind. `married_to` at least has stable surface vocabulary ("wedded", "wife of"), so it is the natural next sibling.

| Iliad 11.465 | **11.456** | DEV-122, GAP-007 resolution, promotion_log rationale |
| Iliad 15.445 | **15.442** | DEV-122, GAP-002 bucket-2 entry |
| Iliad 11.750 | **11.737** | GAP-007 resolution (the Moliones) |
| Odyssey 1.429 | **1.421** | DEV-122 |
| Odyssey 15.249 / 2.38 | **15.238** / **2.35** | GAP-002 bucket-2 entry |

All corrected. One more was found in **DEV-121**, predating this work and left by a different pass: `Oïleus killed_by Agamemnon` is cited as Iliad **11.93**, actually **11.84**. Corrected in place rather than left standing.

**This is the same defect class as GAP-008** — a true claim attached to a citation that does not point where it says. The irony is the point: a pass that built a check for misattributed provenance in the *data* introduced eight instances of it in the *prose*, because prose citations have no check at all. `passage_ref` values in the candidate JSON are safe (they are copied from the extraction segment and now verified by A13); free-text references in `docs/` are not, and nothing verifies them. Worth a lint if this recurs — the corpus files carry the `[n]` markers needed to resolve any `Book.line` pair mechanically, which is exactly how these eight were caught.

### DEV-124 — A14: `variant_claims` gets its first source-grounded check; 108 reversed parentage claims found mechanically and rejected, all 209 rows, with zero false positives

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | Post-P4, tenth of DEV-115's carried-forward items — DEV-123's finding (3), reframed once measured. |
| **Original Plan** | DEV-123 filed this as "A11's recall fix has not been re-measured against the `variant_claims` half — DEV-114/F3 used the same comma-dependent reading of the patronymic, so if that triage shared the assumption its recall is understated by the same bug." |
| **What Changed** | **The premise was wrong and the real gap is larger.** DEV-114's triage shared no code with A11 — it was done by hand in `02_verify_conflicts.ipynb`, so there was no faulty assumption to inherit. Measuring it instead showed the actual state: **A11, A12 and A13 all guard `relationships`, and `variant_claims` — the table the product's defining feature reads — had no source-grounded check of any kind**, while carrying **4,825 unreviewed `parentage` claims**. The reversed shape had been found there twice, both times by hand (DEV-114's batch, DEV-122's ten Telamon rows), which is exactly what an unchecked table looks like from the outside. So the work became a new check rather than a re-measurement. **A14 (`audit/claim_direction.py`, 16 tests)** applies A11's rule to claims. The extra work is that a claim's parent is **free text**: `parse_parent` requires one of four `<child\|son\|daughter\|offspring> of …` prefixes — **4,840 of 5,046 rows (96%)** — then takes the **first** confirmed entity name in the remainder, which is what makes `"child of Ajax son of Telamon"` resolve to Ajax rather than Telamon. **Unresolvable values are counted, not guessed** (493 of them): the `"sprung from Zeus"` formula, whose defect class is GAP-007's and already deny-listed, and 179 free-prose rows. **Those prose rows exposed a modelling issue worth recording separately:** values like *"Mother of the nine Muses by Zeus"* have the **subject as the parent**, so `parentage` conflates "X's parent is Y" with "X is parent of Y" — feeding them to a direction check would invert the question. **Tier handling is deliberately non-uniform**: `trust_tier=2` skipped (a human already decided that row, DEV-113 — re-reporting asks them to re-litigate it), `trust_tier=1` checked and reported *because* those are live in V12, `trust_tier=3` the point of the exercise. **`birth` is normalized to `parentage`** via the V9_2 alias; reading `claim_type` literally would have silently skipped 8 rows. |
| **Reason** | The user picked it off a ranked list, where it ranked first for reusing already-built, already-tested machinery to reach the one table with no coverage — and for converting a 4,825-row hand-review backlog into something filterable. |
| **Impact** | **One new check + a review verdict; no application code, no schema, no migration, and no seeded change at all.** Files: `ingestion/audit/claim_direction.py` (**new**), `ingestion/audit/tests/test_claim_direction.py` (**new**, 16 tests), `variant_claims_candidates.json` (**209 rows** `trust_tier` 3→2; distribution now `{3: 6757, 1: 328, 2: 344}`), `audit/promotion_log.json` (+1 rejection batch, keyed for unit revert), `audit/README.md` (A14 section, count 13 → 14). **First sweep: 108 findings across 1,156 subject+source groups, 0 of them promoted.** **Every finding was reviewed per row — not sampled — against the matched phrase A14 extracted from its own cited source, and all 108 are clean patronymic reversals with zero false positives**: `Cronus \| child of Zeus` against Homer's *"Zeus, son of Cronos"*, `Leto \| child of Apollo` against *"Apollo, son of Leto"*, `Laertes \| child of Odysseus` against *"Odysseus, son of Laertes"*. Two forms confirm today's other work is load-bearing: `Heracles \| child of Antiochus` resolved only through the `Hercules`→`Heracles` alias, and `Agenor \| child of Echeclus` matched only via the **possessive** pattern DEV-123 added to A11 hours earlier. The 108 triples covered **209 rows**, all rejected. **A14 now PASSes.** **V10/V11/V12 regenerated byte-identical** — every rejected row was tier 3, so nothing reaches runtime and the live DB is untouched. **Suites**: ingestion **382** (was 366; +16). |
| **Date** | 2026-07-29 |

**Eval deliberately not run, and this is a deviation from the standing loop stated rather than skipped.** TODO2's cross-cutting rule requires `seedgen --strict` → `reseed-local.sh` → `audit` → eval → `compare.py` before any candidate-JSON edit is committed. Here `seedgen --strict` produced **byte-identical V10/V11/V12**, so no reseed was needed and the live DB is bit-for-bit what DEV-123's 88% run measured. There is no path from a `trust_tier` 3→2 edit on a never-promoted row to runtime behaviour. Re-running would re-measure identical data; if a reviewer wants the belt-and-braces run anyway, it is a 20-minute command and nothing here depends on its outcome.

**Findings this pass did not fix:**

1. **`parentage` conflates two opposite relations — a latent trap, NOT live.** The free-prose values include rows where the subject is the *parent* ("Mother of the nine Muses by Zeus", "Father of Athena by Metis"). A14 leaves them unchecked because a direction check on them asks the wrong question, but the underlying issue is a claim-type modelling gap, not a parser limitation. **Corrected 2026-07-29, same day:** this entry first said "a *who were X's parents?* answer can today include claims about X's *children*", which overstated it — measured afterwards, there are **29** such rows and **all 29 are `trust_tier=3`**, so none is in V12 and no answer can reach one. The real exposure is a **promotion-time trap**: nothing stops a future reviewer promoting one, and `ConflictSynthesizer` would then present it alongside genuine parent claims for the same subject. A cheap guard — refuse to promote a `parentage` row whose value is subject-as-parent shaped — belongs with whoever next works the promotion workflow.
2. **493 unresolvable claim values remain unchecked** — 179 prose plus the rest failing the four-prefix requirement. No estimate of how many hide a reversal.
3. **A14 covers `parentage` only.** `death` (943 claims) and `marriage` (676) have no check; `marriage` is symmetric so direction is meaningless there, but `death` has the same killer/victim asymmetry A12 handles for `relationships`.
4. **The 108 rejections were not cross-checked against `relationships`.** Where a reversed claim has a `relationships` counterpart, A11 should have caught it independently; A11 reports 0, so either the counterparts are absent or A11's `correct == 0` abstained on them. Which, is unmeasured — and it is the obvious way to estimate A11's true recall.

**Addendum to DEV-124, 2026-07-29 — a second verification pass (asked whether every finding was written down) found one A14 defect and one new data class, neither previously recorded.**

5. **A14 silently swallows self-referential claims instead of reporting them — a defect in the check as shipped.** `find_reversed_claims` contains `if parent is None or parent == subject: continue`, written to stop a subject being compared against itself. It works, but `continue` means those rows are **dropped from the output entirely** rather than surfaced, so a claim asserting someone is their own parent can never be flagged by the only check that looks at these rows. The guard should split: skip the *direction* comparison (which is meaningless) but emit a finding of its own kind.

6. **52 self-referential claims exist, and 42 have never been reviewed.** Measured, not assumed: `subject_name` equal to the parsed parent or killer gives **35 `parentage`** and **17 `death`** rows — `Cronus | death | killed by Cronus`, `Perses | parentage | child of Perses`, `Orpheus | parentage | child of Orpheus`, `Aeolus | parentage | child of Aeolus`. **42 are `trust_tier=3`; 10 are already `trust_tier=2`**, which is itself informative — earlier reviewers caught some of these by hand, exactly the pattern (a defect found repeatedly by hand and never mechanically) that justified A12 and A14 in the first place. **None is promoted**, so nothing is live. The detection rule is one equality comparison, which makes this the cheapest unworked item currently on the board.

### DEV-126 — A14/A15 now resolve claim names through the curated alias map; 209 rows became checkable and surfaced a reversal that had been reviewed under its other spelling

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | Post-P4, thirteenth of DEV-115's carried-forward items — DEV-125's finding (2) ("`death` still has 345 unparsed values and `parentage` 492 — no estimate of how many hide a defect"), answered by measurement rather than another sweep. |
| **Original Plan** | None. DEV-125 left the unparsed residue as an unquantified backlog; this entry measures it, finds that a large decidable slice needed no new judgment at all, and closes that slice. |
| **What Changed** | **`parse_parent` (A14) and `parse_killer` (A15) matched claim values against the confirmed entity names only** — never against `known_aliases.json` or the live `entity_aliases` table, **the same two-layer map A1 has read since B3**. So both checks were blind to any claim phrased in a translation variant the project had **already curated**. Not a small tail: `child of Cronos` alone is **114 rows**, on the most genealogically central Titan in the corpus, plus `Ocean`→Oceanus (21), `Jupiter` (11), `Saturn` (8), `Athene` (5), `Ulysses`→Odysseus (9). Both parsers now share one `_resolve_name` helper that widens the candidate set with alias spellings and returns the **canonical** name — required, not tidy, since the caller compares the result against `subject_name` and hands it to `_attests`, both of which speak canonical. `names_self` resolves too, so a suicide written `Ajax \| killed by Aias` is recognised instead of read as an ordinary two-party claim. **Two guards were written for cases that do not exist in today's data** — a dangling alias whose canonical is unconfirmed, and an alias key that is itself a confirmed entity — because the alternative is a silent misresolution the first time a batch adds one; both are pinned by tests. **The `Saturn`/`Jupiter` rows are fallout from our own DEV-121 merge**: that pass made them entity aliases, but the claim *values* still say `Saturn`, so A14 went blind to eight rows at the moment the merge landed. |
| **Reason** | The user picked this off a ranked list of open data gaps. It was chosen over the larger backlogs (GAP-002's 347 names, GAP-001's ~690 dropped parents) because it invents no data and makes no new judgment calls: every name comes from a map a human already curated, so the whole change is mechanical, and it strengthens the only checks guarding the table the product's defining feature reads. |
| **Impact** | **Two audit checks + tests + a four-row rejection; no application code, no schema, no migration, no seeded change.** Files: `ingestion/audit/claim_direction.py` (`_resolve_name`, `_self_surface_forms`, `_matches_self`, `load_name_aliases`, threaded through `find_reversed_claims`/`count_unparsed`/`run`), `ingestion/audit/death_direction.py` (same, importing the shared helpers), `ingestion/audit/tests/test_claim_direction.py` (+7), `ingestion/audit/tests/test_death_direction.py` (+6), `variant_claims_candidates.json` (**4 rows** 3→2; distribution now `{3: 6695, 1: 328, 2: 406}`), `audit/promotion_log.json` (+1 rejection batch `a14-alias-resolved-athene-reversal`), `audit/README.md` (A14/A15 sections). **Unparsed: A14 492 → 298, A15 345 → 330 — 209 rows became checkable**, matching the pre-flight estimate exactly. **A14 found one new reversal, A15 none.** Suites: ingestion **417** (was 404; +13). `seedgen --strict` regenerated **V10/V11/V12 byte-identical** (md5-verified before and after); full `python -m audit` ends **PASS or WAIVED on every check except A3's 86 candidate-layer cycles** — identical to the pre-pass gate state, and A3 is untouched here (`relationships_candidates_cleaned.json` unmodified). |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**The finding that matters is not the row, it is what sat beside it.** A14's new hit is `Zeus | parentage | child of Athene` — false on its face, and the cited passage says so in its own first line (*"Athene, daughter of Zeus that beareth the aegis"*, Iliad 5.733). But the **six sibling rows spelling her `Athena` had already been reviewed and rejected to `trust_tier=2` by an earlier hand pass**. The identical false claim was therefore caught on one spelling and structurally unreviewable on the other, for as long as both checks have existed. That asymmetry — not the single row — is the defect this pass removes, and it is the same seeded-vs-review-gated shape DEV-118 argued in general, one layer down: a human gate only protects what the check can put in front of it.

All four `Athene` rows were verified per row against their own cited passage before rejection, and they did **not** turn out to be one shape: Hymns 5.7 and Iliad 5.733 state the correct direction outright, Iliad 21.416 names Zeus's actual father (*"Zeus, son of Cronos"*), and Iliad 5.864-5.907 states **no parentage at all** — that one is unsupported by its own citation (the DEV-098 shape), not reversed. Rejecting it is right either way, but recording it as a reversal would have been wrong.

**Findings this pass did not fix** (the DEV-115/119/121/122 discipline, run before writing this entry):

1. **The residue is now characterised, and it is mostly not name-resolution.** Of A14's remaining 298, only **96** have a valid `<child> of …` prefix with an unresolvable name; **202** are free prose or the Homeric formula, which A14's design deliberately excludes. Of A15's 330, **68** vs **262**. So a further alias batch would reach at most ~96 and ~68 rows — the rest need a different technique, not a bigger map.
2. **The fuzzy scan that found this is a lead list, not a fix list.** Scoring the unresolvable names against the confirmed set at 80–100 surfaces real pairs (`Erectheus`/`Erechtheus` 94.7, `Peirithous`/`Pirithous` 94.7, `Arceisius`/`Arcisius` 94.1, `Ortilochus`/`Orsilochus` 90.0) **mixed with confident false pairs between genuinely distinct figures** (`Alcmene`→`Alcimenes` 87.5, `Venus`→`Venulus`, `Phorcus`→`Phocus`, `Arion`→`Orion`, `Laius`→`Latinus`). None was acted on. Each is an alias decision needing the GAP-002 bucket-2 namesake guard, exactly as DEV-122 established when it discarded the `Peisenor`/`Cleitus` aliases.
3. **A1's 83-86 cluster gains a fourth member.** `Erectheus`/`Erechtheus` and `Peirithous`/`Pirithous` both score **94.7** — above A1's 88 threshold — yet appear only inside *claim values*, never as competing entity names, so A1 structurally cannot see them. DEV-121's finding (4) argued for a diacritic-folding pre-pass on A1; this adds that A1's input set is itself too narrow, which folding would not fix.
4. **`Chryseis` is confirmed missing from the entity set**, closing the open question in DEV-125's finding (4): the `Chryses | daughter of Chryses` name-collapse rejected there has no `Chryseis` entity to have been extracted correctly into. A genuine GAP-002 instance, verified not assumed, and left for that gap's triage.
5. **The alias map is loaded but its DB layer is never exercised offline.** `load_name_aliases` reads `known_aliases.json` (58 entries) always and the live `entity_aliases` table (58 rows) only when a DB connection exists. The two currently agree, so no drift is visible — but nothing checks that they agree, and a future migration adding an alias to only one would go unnoticed.
6. **A7 has the same alias blindness this pass just fixed in A14/A15 — in the one place it was built to protect.** Found by a verification pass after the work was written up (asked whether every finding had been recorded), not during it. `name_coverage.py` scores a confirmed entity by `corpus_counts.get(base, 0)`, crediting only the **canonical** spelling, so every figure the translations render under an alias is undercounted: `Heracles` 29 canonical vs **201** as `Hercules`, `Ajax` 46 vs **177** as `Aias`, `Athena` 222 vs 174 as `Athene`, `Apollo` 336 vs 139 as `Phoebus`. Three canonical names fall **below A7's 10-mention threshold** entirely because of it — `Cronus` (9 canonical / **195** as `Cronos`), `Ouranos` (**0** / 72 as `Heaven`), `Helius` (6 / 32 as `Helios`) — so A7 cannot flag them at any row count. **Measured before being reported as live: no finding is currently suppressed**, because all three still have candidate relationship rows (111 / 54 / 6) and A7's rule needs `max_rows=0`. The hole is therefore **latent, not active** — but it sits exactly in A7's own use case: the check exists because DEV-098 found `Ares` **totally erased** from the candidate rows, and if that happened tomorrow to `Cronus`, `Ouranos`, or `Helius`, A7 would be silent. A7 is the only check that counts corpus tokens, so this bounds the class; A1 already reads the alias map, and A14/A15 now do. **FIXED 2026-07-30 (DEV-127).**
7. **`python -m audit --candidates` silently corrupts A10's drift baseline, and it is a tracked file.** Found by accident here rather than by design: running the no-DB mode to verify this change degrades gracefully rewrote `audit/group_inventory_baseline.json`'s `lastZeroPromoted` from **725 to 749**. **Root cause, reproduced against a throwaway baseline rather than inferred:** `run()` sets `claim_type_alias_map = load_alias_map(db_conn) if db_conn is not None else {}` (`group_inventory.py:214`), so without a DB the `claim_type` surface variants never collapse — **838 groups instead of 797**, and 749 zero-promoted instead of 725. `save_baseline` (line 224) then persists that number unconditionally. **Two harms, and the second is the serious one:** (a) the candidates run *itself* emits an `error` finding — *"zero_promoted increased … promotion is monotone, so this means a promotion was lost"* — which is the DEV-101/Track C **corruption signature**, raised here as a pure false alarm; (b) once 749 is persisted, the monotonicity guard is **defeated on every later DB run**, because a genuine lost promotion anywhere up to 749 is no longer greater than the recorded last value and passes silently. A guard that fails open is worse than the phantom alarm. Restored with `git checkout` and re-verified at 725 after a full DB run. Nothing in the README warns that a read-only-sounding invocation mutates committed state; the honest fix is that a run which cannot normalize `claim_type` must not advance the tracker at all. **FIXED 2026-07-30 (DEV-127).**

### DEV-127 — A10's drift tracker no longer fails open on a no-DB run, and A7 counts a figure's alias spellings; both were checks mishandling their own inputs

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | Post-P4, fourteenth of DEV-115's carried-forward items — DEV-126's own findings (6) and (7), both found by that entry's verification pass rather than during its work. |
| **Original Plan** | None. Both are defects in audit checks, found while fixing a third; DEV-126 recorded them and deliberately left them. |
| **What Changed** | **A10 (`group_inventory.py`) — the drift guard failed open, which is worse than the false alarm that revealed it.** `run()` builds its inventory with `claim_type_alias_map = load_alias_map(db_conn) if db_conn is not None else {}`, so a `--candidates` invocation never collapses `claim_type` surface variants: **838 groups instead of 797, 749 zero-promoted instead of 725** (reproduced against a throwaway baseline, not inferred). `save_baseline` then persisted that inflated figure unconditionally, and both baseline-relative findings fired against it — including the DEV-101/Track C **corruption signature**, as a pure false alarm. The silent half was the real damage: once `lastZeroPromoted` held 749, a genuine lost promotion anywhere below it was no longer an *increase*, so **the invariant that exists to catch promotion corruption would never fire again**. `check_invariants` now takes `comparable`; a no-DB run suppresses the two baseline-relative findings, leaves the tracker exactly where it was, and says so in its trend line. The **arithmetic-identity** check stays live in both modes — it is internal to the run and owes nothing to the baseline. **A10's first-run path was worse than DEV-126 described**: with no baseline file present, a no-DB run would have fixed the inflated figure as `zeroPromotedBaseline` *permanently*, with nothing left to compare it against. **A7 (`name_coverage.py`) — alias-blind mention counts.** `corpus_counts.get(base, 0)` credited only the canonical spelling, so the translations' own names went uncounted: `Heracles` 29 vs `Hercules` 201, `Ajax` 46 vs `Aias` 177. `find_uncovered` now takes `name_aliases` and sums a figure's spellings, folding the canonical through `base_name` so the credit lands on the key the count is actually keyed by. |
| **Reason** | The user picked both off a ranked list. They are one pass rather than two: both are audit checks mishandling their inputs, neither touches seeded data, and A7's fix reuses `load_name_aliases` from DEV-126. |
| **Impact** | **Two audit checks + tests; no application code, no schema, no migration, no seeded change, no candidate-data change.** Files: `ingestion/audit/group_inventory.py` (`comparable` parameter, conditional save, corrected `run()` docstring), `ingestion/audit/name_coverage.py` (`name_aliases` parameter, alias-summed mentions, `load_name_aliases` wired into `run()`), `ingestion/audit/tests/test_group_inventory.py` (+4, **1 rewritten**), `ingestion/audit/tests/test_name_coverage.py` (+4), `ingestion/audit/README.md` (A7/A10 sections). Suites: ingestion **425** (was 417; +8). **Live effect on A7's mention counts, measured: `Cronus` 9 → 214, `Ouranos` 0 → 77, `Helius` 6 → 38, `Heracles` 29 → 230, `Ajax` 46 → 223** — all three formerly-sub-threshold names now far clear the floor. **A7's finding count is unchanged at 2 (both waived), exactly as predicted**: the hole was latent, since all three still have candidate relationship rows. `Cronus` gains 214 rather than the 204 DEV-126 projected because `Saturn` maps there too, from the DEV-121 merge. **A10 candidates-mode: FINDINGS → PASS**, baseline md5-identical before and after. Full `python -m audit`: PASS or WAIVED on every check except A3's 86 candidate-layer cycles — identical to the pre-pass gate state. |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**The first fix was incomplete, and this entry's own verification pass caught it.** `save_baseline` is called from **two** places, and the initial fix guarded only `run()` (the aggregate-runner path, which at least accepts a `baseline_path` override). The standalone CLI `python -m audit.group_inventory` has the identical unguarded sequence at `main()` — build with `claim_type_alias_map = {}` when `--db` is absent, then `check_invariants(...)` and `save_baseline(new_baseline)` — and it writes **`DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH` directly, with no override**, so it is the *more* damaging of the two paths. Both are now guarded on the same rule. A regression test covers the CLI path and was **verified to fail without the guard** rather than assumed to cover it: the fix was temporarily reverted, the test failed, and the fix restored. Recording this because the failure mode is instructive — a defect described as "fixed" in a written-up entry, where the write-up was accurate about the mechanism and wrong about the extent.

**An existing test had pinned the defect, and is the most useful thing this entry records.** `test_run_reports_inventory_from_candidates_only` asserted `baseline_path.exists()` after a no-DB run — encoding "a candidates-only run writes the baseline" as *intended* behaviour. It passed continuously while the guard it protects was being disarmed. It is rewritten to assert the opposite, with a comment naming what it used to pin, because a test that passes for the wrong reason is harder to find later than an untested path: nothing about a green suite invites you to look at it. This is the second time in three passes that a check's own machinery, not its data, was the defect (DEV-125's A14 skip was the first).

**A7's blind spot was documented from the start and filed as harmless.** The README's scope limits already named it — *"a translation-name mismatch is a known false-negative (Ovid says `Mars`), **which is the safe direction** — it under-counts mentions and so under-flags."* The mechanism was understood; the severity was misjudged. Under-flagging is not the safe direction for a check whose whole purpose is detecting an absence, and the measurements above show why: it did not merely lower three entities' scores, it put them **under the floor**, disabling the check for them entirely. This is a different failure from DEV-126's, where nobody had noticed the gap at all — here it was written down and reasoned about, and the reasoning was wrong. Worth more than the fix: a documented limitation carries an implicit severity claim, and *"it only under-flags"* deserves the same scepticism as an undocumented gap when the check exists to find things that are missing.

**Findings this pass did not fix** (verification pass run before writing this entry, not after being asked):

1. **The other two audit modes are unexamined for the same class.** This entry fixed `--candidates` for A10 by asking what its inputs cannot support. `--db` was never audited the same way: several checks (A2, A4) report both a `candidates:` and a `db:` figure, and nothing verifies that a `--db`-only run degrades as deliberately as a candidates-only one now does. No defect is claimed here — the question simply has not been asked.
1b. **A10 is the only check that mutates committed state from `run()`, verified rather than assumed.** Every other `write_text` in the package sits in a `main()` CLI path behind an `--output` argument. Those defaults *are* tracked files (`name_coverage_findings.json`, `duplicate_entities_findings.json`, …), so those CLIs do overwrite committed artifacts — but that is their stated purpose and the write is a **report**, not a **tracker**: re-running reproduces it, and nothing downstream compares against the previous value. A10's baseline is different in kind, which is why only it could fail open.
2. **A7's `min_mentions=10` floor was never re-justified after the counts changed.** The threshold was chosen when mentions were undercounted by up to 201 for a single figure. **Measured: 308 → 313 entities now clear the floor (+5)**, so the effect is a slightly *noisier* check, not a quieter one. (An earlier draft of this entry asserted the opposite — that the floor would make the check quieter — and called it "the opposite of the usual threshold risk." That was backwards: raising every count makes a fixed floor easier to clear, not harder. Corrected here by measurement rather than left standing.) The practical effect today is nil, since A7 also requires zero candidate rows and its finding count held at 2 — but the floor's justification is now stale, whichever direction it moves.
3. **`entity_aliases` and `known_aliases.json` still have no cross-check** — DEV-126 finding (5), untouched here and now load-bearing for one more check. A7 reads the JSON layer only (it takes no `db_conn`), so a future alias added solely by migration would silently fail to credit mentions.

### DEV-128 — Stage P5 re-scoped: corpus-complete seeding of the existing tables comes first, the review axis changes from subject to passage, and two standing rules are added to stop the drift that prompted the review

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | P5, before any P5 work started. Prompted by a review of documented data gaps and open TODOs, asked for because recent minor fixes appeared to be generating more minor problems. |
| **Original Plan** | `TODO2.md` Stage P5 — "New data types & systematic gap discovery" — as three sub-stages: **P5a** numeric data (`contingents`, activating ADR-009), **P5b** myths & participants (grow beyond 5 myths; Trojan cycle for Q11), **P5c** geography/epithets. The tables that already exist were assumed adequately seeded; P5's job was to add *new* kinds of data. |
| **What Changed** | **(1) P5-0 inserted ahead of P5a/b/c and owns the stage:** corpus-complete seeding of the tables that already exist. **(2) The review scoping axis changes from subject prominence to passage.** P4's F0a tranche rule (DEV-109) ranks review by A8 subject prominence; because major figures are named everywhere, that pays nearly the full corpus-reading cost for a fraction of the rows. Measured: the top-20-subject tranche costs **750 passage reads to reach 2,544** tier-3 rows (3.4 rows/read), while **all 1,059 passages reach all 6,695** (6.3 rows/read) — 2.6× the rows for 1.4× the reads. (First written as "753 reads to reach 2,621"; corrected per DEV-129, which also records the construction.) The backlog was never 6,695 row decisions — it is **1,059 passage reads**, ~424,000 words. **(3) A coverage metric (`A16`) becomes the stage's exit criterion**, so "are we drifting?" is answerable in one command instead of inferred from 15 checks, 8 GAPs and 127 DEV entries. **(4) A detector budget** — one new `audit/` check per 250 net rows seeded, with check *bugfixes* spending the same budget. **(5) The findings rule** — a five-class routing decision for defects surfaced mid-work. **(6) P5b frozen**, replaced by a written coverage statement. **(7) ADR-004 Amendment 1 planned** (P5-0 Track B7) to sanction evidence-assisted batch approval. |
| **Reason** | Measured drift, not a hunch. `ingestion/audit/promotion_log.json`: 2026-07-28 (P4 tracks F0–F3) promoted **253 rows**. The following two days — 7 commits, checks A12–A15 plus two rounds of fixes *to those checks* — **promoted 4 rows** and rejected 286. The user-visible database gained essentially nothing. Meanwhile `variant_claims` sits at **6.3% row coverage / 8.1% conflict-group coverage** (300 seeded of a 4,743-row reachable ceiling; **723 of 795 groups have zero promoted rows**). Adding new data types on top of a 6%-seeded differentiator table optimises the wrong thing. ⚠️ **Four figures in this row were corrected on 2026-07-30 — see DEV-129.** As first written it read "299 seeded of 7,429 candidates", "4% row coverage / ~7% conflict-group coverage", "749 of 838 groups", and "every rejected row at `trust_tier=3`, i.e. never seeded". The direction of the argument is unchanged and the re-scope stands. |
| **Impact** | **Documentation only in this commit — no code, no schema, no migration, no seeded-data change, no candidate-data change.** Files: `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` (new; 6 tracks A–F, ~35 items, standing-rules block), `docs/TODO2.md` (Stage P5 re-scoped with a deviation banner; P5b marked `[~]`; the dangling `TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` pointer at line 555 now resolves; two rules appended to `## Cross-cutting rules`), `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` (this entry). No `.py`, `.kt`, `.sql` or `.json` file is touched. ADR-009 stays **Proposed** — P5a is now sequenced after P5-0, so its acceptance moves with it. |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**The drift had a mechanical cause, and blaming discipline would have been the wrong diagnosis.** Every one of DEV-118 through DEV-127 is defensible work: A11 fixed 72 reversed edges, A14 found 108 reversed parentage claims with zero false positives, DEV-127 closed a guard that failed open. The problem is not that they were wrong, it is that the subject-prominence tranche had run out of cheap subjects — P4's F3 closed the top-20 backlog outright at 20/20 — and with the queue exhausted, detector-building became the available work. **The same rule also produced 602 of the 649 A6 waivers**, whose stated reason is "this row's child is outside the frozen top-20 list". That is a scoping decision recorded as a waiver, and it is why P5-0 Track A6 revokes those rather than triaging them: the rows were never judged, only deferred by an axis that is itself being replaced. ⚠️ **Corrected per DEV-129:** this first read "the 649 A6 waivers", and Track A6 was written to revoke all of them. **47 are not scope-shaped** — they are DEV-119 per-row triage verdicts against cited passages ("the dropped rival is ALREADY represented among this child's promoted claims", "the cited passage contains NO parentage claim", "already reviewed and REJECTED", "a GENUINE variant tradition"). Revoking those would have discarded real review work and re-opened decided rows.

**The two rules exist because recording was already good and routing was absent.** This repo has an unusually strong convention for writing down defects it is not fixing — the "Findings this pass did not fix" sections run to a dozen numbered items in recent entries, and DEV-127's verification pass caught its own incomplete fix. What no rule covered is what happens *next*: the observed pattern is record it, then fix it in the following commit, which is how DEV-125's A14 repair led to DEV-126's alias work led to DEV-127's guard fix. Applied retroactively, **DEV-125 through DEV-127 were all class 3 or class 4 findings treated as class 1** — none of them touched seeded data, so under the findings rule all three would have been recorded against a queue position and the intervening two days spent on passages instead. The rule does not say they were not worth fixing; it says they were not worth fixing *then*.

**Why the coverage metric is group-based, not row-based.** A16's headline number for `variant_claims` counts `(subject, canonical claim_type)` groups holding ≥2 distinct `source_id` **and** ≥2 distinct `claim_value` — an actual surfaceable conflict — not promoted rows. Row counts are gameable in a way that would have flattered the existing work: promoting six epithets of one god moves the row number by six and the product by nothing. Group coverage is what a user experiences when they ask a conflict-shaped question. **DEV-129 adds a second, stronger reason discovered after this entry was written:** the row denominator is not reachable at all. `seedgen` can seed at most 4,743 of the 7,429 candidates (359 lost to absent subjects, 2,327 to a 4-tuple dedup omitting `passage_ref`), where the *group* ceiling is 715 of 764 — 93.6%. The metric chosen for presentation reasons turns out to be the only one of the two that can reach ~100%.

**Findings this pass did not fix** (the DEV-115/119/121/122 discipline, run before writing this entry):

1. **The 649 A6 waivers are still in `audit-waivers.json` and still suppressing findings.** Track A6 revokes them; until it runs, `python -m audit` reports A6 as WAIVED on rows that were never judged. The gap between "this entry says they are a backlog" and "the file still calls them waivers" is real and is deliberately not closed here, because this commit is documentation-only.
2. **ADR-004 is not yet amended, so evidence-assisted batch approval is not sanctioned.** P5-0 Track B7 owns it, and Track B's exit criterion requires the amendment to merge *before* any batch approval is used. Anyone starting Track C before B7 lands would be promoting rows under a gate definition that does not yet permit the method.
3. **A draft of this entry quoted three wrong seeded counts, which is the argument for A16 and E3 in miniature.** The checklist was first written with `entities` 1,986 / `relationships` 3,360 / `variant_claims` 299, taken from an exploration pass over the migrations. The migrations actually hold **1,990 / 3,367 / 300** (`grep -cE "^\s*\("` over V10/V11/V12), and the live DB agrees with them — so there is no migration-vs-DB drift, just a miscount that survived into a draft because nothing recomputes these figures. Caught by the plan's own verification step and corrected before commit. The lesson is not that the numbers were wrong once — it is that a hand-quoted count has no mechanism telling anyone when it stops being true, which is what A16 is for and why Track E3 stops new DEV entries from restating counts at all.

   ⚠️ **This item then claimed too much, and DEV-129 corrects it.** As committed it continued: *"Every candidate-side figure in the same documents (7,429 candidates; tier1 328 / tier2 406 / tier3 6,695; 838 groups; 749 zero-promoted; 1,059 tier-3 passages; 2,229 / 3,673 / 5,183 rows at the 100 / 250 / 500-passage marks) was verified against the live tree and is exact."* Most of that list is exact — but **838 / 749 are the alias-blind group figures** (A10 as it runs reports **795 / 723**), and the neighbouring `2,621 / 753` subject-axis pair is unreproducible under any construction. An entry warning that hand-quoted counts go stale, asserting exactness over a figure that was already wrong, is the cleanest possible argument for E3.
4. **`myths`/`myth_participants` are frozen on a value judgement, not a measurement.** There is no candidate pool to measure against, so unlike every other table in the coverage report there is no denominator and no honest percentage — A16 prints `n/a` for them by design. The freeze rests on the argument that a 5-row table in the text-to-SQL schema prompt is a liability, which is reasoning, not evidence. If a later gold question needs structured myth participation, this decision is the first thing to revisit.
5. **The 82%-noise result that killed A13 was never re-examined under passage scoping.** A13's construction-matching half failed because it checked citations against whole sources. B3's bucketing checks each row against *its own cited passage segment*, which is a materially narrower question — and the bucket-A measurement during this review suggested the narrow form is clean. That does not resurrect A13, and E1 explicitly forbids revisiting GAP-008 with a wider regex; it does mean the recorded dead end is narrower than "citation verification does not work".

### DEV-129 — DEV-128's own figures and Stage P5's track arithmetic corrected against the live tree, before any P5 work started

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | P5-0, after DEV-128 landed and before any of its tracks began. Prompted by a verification review of the DEV-128 commit, asked for because the re-scope's whole argument is quantitative and none of its numbers had a recorded construction. |
| **Original Plan** | DEV-128 plus `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` and `docs/TODO2.md` Stage P5 as committed 2026-07-30: `variant_claims` at "4% row / ~7% conflict-group coverage (300 of 7,429; 749 of 838 groups)"; subject axis at "753 passage reads to reach 2,621 rows"; rejections "at `trust_tier=3`"; Track A6 revoking "the 649 A6 waivers"; Track A7 making `load_waivers` reject scope-shaped waivers; Track D1 bounded to "the top-20 unknown names by reference count" with exits ≥53% edge / ≥87% name-space; Track E1 "A1–A15 is enough"; Track C's per-batch loop ending in a bare `python -m audit --only A16`. |
| **What Changed** | Seven corrections, each measured. **(1) The `variant_claims` row denominator is unreachable.** `seedgen/variant_claims_gen.py::_reviewed_rows` silently (bare `continue`) drops rows whose subject is absent from `entities` and collapses the 4-tuple `(subject, claim_type, claim_value, source_id)`, which **omits `passage_ref`**. Promoting all 7,429 candidates through that filter yields **4,743 rows** — a 63.8% ceiling. Real coverage is 300/4,743 = **6.3%**, not 4%, and ~35% of Track C's adjudication effort produces no DB row for reasons unrelated to the reviewer. New Track A2a reports the ceiling by calling `_reviewed_rows` itself, so it can never drift from what seedgen does. **(2) `838 groups / 749 zero-promoted` are the alias-blind figures.** `build_group_inventory(cands, {}, None)` returns exactly 838/749; with the `claim_type` and entity-alias maps A10 actually passes, it returns **795/723**. The "~7%" was a mixed-layer ratio (62 alias-resolved ÷ 838 alias-blind); under A16's own stated definition it is **62/764 = 8.1%**. **(3) `2,621 rows / 753 passages` is unreproducible** — top-20-by-composite gives 2,544/750 (alias resolution changes nothing), top-21 gives 2,601/758, top-20-by-`mentionCount` gives 2,590/753. Replaced with 2,544/750 **and the construction that produced it**. **(4) Rejection writes `trust_tier=2`, not 3** (1 = promoted, 2 = checked-and-rejected, 3 = never reviewed; 120 + 286 = 406 = today's tier-2 count) — and "the rejected rows never seeded" is a tautology, so the sentence proved less than it appeared to. **(5) Track A7 as written crashed the entire suite.** `load_waivers` (`audit/__main__.py:52`) **raises `ValueError`**, and `main()` calls it unconditionally at line 199 *before* `--only` filtering — so rejecting scope-shaped waivers while the 347 A2 scope entries remain kills every `python -m audit` invocation, including `--only A16`, which is Track A's own exit criterion. E5 is resequenced to run first, and A7a keys the filter off the reason prefix. **(6) Track A6 would have destroyed 47 real review decisions** — 602 of the 649 A6 waivers are scope-shaped (`F0b/F0c …`), 47 are DEV-119 per-row triage verdicts against cited passages. Now revokes 602. **(7) Track D's exits were unreachable within Track D's own bound:** rank 1 of the "top-20 unknown names" is the placeholder `<UNKNOWN>` (133 refs) and 6 more are excluded by D4, leaving **13 workable names → +116 edges → 50.6% / 85.7%** against exits of ≥53% / ≥87% (which need +280 edges and +43 entities ⚠️ **+44 — corrected per
DEV-132**; `0.87 × 2,337 = 2,033.2`, so +43 lands at 86.99%). The exits were the right targets, so the **bound** rises: D1 now works the first **60 eligible** names (placeholders and D4 exclusions removed) → projected **+299 edges → 53.3% / 87.7%**, with the 60th name still at 3 references, clear of the 192 singletons. Plus: new Track A9 strips `<UNKNOWN>` from the A8 and A2 rankings (it sat at **rank 19 by composite**, so it was one of the 20 subjects P4's F3 "closed 20/20"); new bucket Z in B3 classifies the **354 tier-3 rows whose subject is absent from `entities`** before they cost a read (108 junk subjects, 80 blocked by D4's decision, ~166 recoverable via Track D); B2 gains the alias-map shape adapter (`_spellings` consumes `dict[str, set[str]]`, `load_name_aliases` produces `dict[str, str]`; feeding one to the other raises `TypeError`) and B2a the `entity_aliases`↔`known_aliases.json` cross-check that bucket D and C5 depend on; B7 gains the clause binding batch **rejection** by the same evidence rule as batch approval; E1 admits A16 and the seeding rule gains a standing exemption for findings-free instruments (the budget otherwise forbade A16, the stage's own serial gate, at 0 net rows since A15); the seeding rule is scoped to seeding batches (it otherwise read as violated by ~22 of ~35 items); and Track C's loop gains `--out` on the A16 run, because both invocations write the same date-derived `reports/<today>.md` and the second was overwriting the 16-check report with a one-check one. |
| **Reason** | The re-scope's argument is entirely quantitative, and DEV-128 explicitly staked its credibility on the figures being exact ("verified against the live tree and is exact"). Two of them were not, and one of the two was alias-blind — the same defect class DEV-126 had fixed two days earlier and which DEV-128 cites approvingly. Separately, three tracks could not have executed as written: A7 would have crashed the suite, A6 would have discarded 47 verdicts, and Track D could not have met its own exit criteria. All seven were found by re-deriving each figure from the code and data rather than reading the prose. |
| **Impact** | **Documentation only — no code, no schema, no migration, no seeded-data change, no candidate-data change.** Files: `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` (corrections inline and marked; new items A2a, A9, A7a, B2a, bucket Z, a *Track order* block; D1's bound and C5's scope narrowed), `docs/TODO2.md` (Stage P5 banner and P5-0 summary refigured; seeding rule scoped and given the instrument exemption; a third cross-cutting rule added), `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` (DEV-128's Reason/What-Changed/finding-3/A6-waiver passages annotated in place per the append-only convention — the original wording is quoted wherever it was superseded; this entry). **The re-scope itself stands unchanged**: the passage axis still reaches 2.6× the rows for 1.4× the reads, group coverage is still the right headline (and now for a second reason — it is the only one of the two metrics that can reach ~100%), and P5b stays frozen. |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**The single most useful number this review produced is a ceiling, not a correction.** `variant_claims` cannot exceed **4,743 rows** from the current candidate pool, and its surfaceable-conflict groups cannot exceed **715 of 764**. Without that stated up front, Track C's first sprint would have adjudicated ~2,229 rows, seeded perhaps 1,400, and reported a shortfall the reviewer could neither explain nor fix — which under the seeding rule's "a batch closes only on coverage moving" is indistinguishable from the drift the stage exists to stop. The ceiling is also the reason the group metric survives scrutiny: 93% of groups are reachable where only 64% of rows are.

**Two of the seven corrections were self-inflicted by the same mechanism the stage is built to remove.** A7's crash and E1's "A1–A15 is enough" both come from writing a rule and a task in the same document without executing either. The findings rule was supposed to stop mid-batch detector work; it says nothing about *checking that a planned item runs*, which is what a dry read of `load_waivers` would have caught in a minute. Track A's exit criterion is now explicitly "both `python -m audit` and `python -m audit --only A16` still exit cleanly", so the suite's own health is a gate rather than an assumption.

**Findings this pass did not fix:**

1. **`entity_aliases` and `known_aliases.json` still have no cross-check** — DEV-126 finding (5), carried forward by DEV-128, and now load-bearing for a third thing: B3's bucket D. It is homed at Track B2a and gates C5, but it is not done, and until it is, no bucket-D row may be batch-rejected. `parentage_direction.load_aliases` reads the DB table only; `claim_direction.load_name_aliases` reads the JSON layer too. Any adjudication path taking the former alone is alias-blind by construction.
2. **The 2,327-row dedup collapse is recorded as a ceiling, not investigated as a choice.** Dropping `passage_ref` from the identity key means the same claim attested in two passages of one source seeds once, keeping whichever `passage_ref` came first in candidate order. That is a provenance loss in the exact field DEV-021 added so surfaced conflicts could cite like RAG answers. Whether the key *should* include `passage_ref` — which would raise the ceiling from 4,743 to **7,036** and change `variant_claims` from one-row-per-claim to one-row-per-attestation — is a real design question this entry does not open, and the F1 coverage statement is instructed to describe the loss rather than resolve it.
3. **The 649→602/47 waiver split was measured by reason-string prefix**, which works today because DEV-119 wrote two distinct prefixes. It is not a durable classification: a future waiver phrased differently would be misfiled by A7a's filter. A structured `scope: true` field would be the honest fix and is not proposed here, because it would touch `audit-waivers.json`'s schema and this commit is documentation-only. ⚠️ **This was not a future risk — see DEV-130 correction (4).** Two of the 47 keepers already carry neither prefix (`GAP-007 / DEV-122:` and `DEV-122:`), so the misfiling was live in this file at the moment this finding was written. A7a now keys off the **revoke** side (`F0b`/`F0c`), which removes the hazard without the schema change.
4. **A13 (`passage_support.py`) is still in the suite** as a recorded dead end, still running on every invocation, still counted among the checks. E1 forbids revisiting GAP-008 but no item retires the module, so the detector suite's maintenance surface — the thing the budget exists to bound — still includes a check nobody trusts.
5. **`<UNKNOWN>` was rank 19 for an unknown length of time.** A9 removes it, but P4's F3 recorded "top-20 backlog closed 20/20" with a placeholder occupying one of the 20 slots, and this entry does not go back to establish what that did to F3's completion claim or to the 602 waivers scoped by that list.

### DEV-130 — Five execution-blocking contradictions in the Stage P5 checklist fixed: the waiver relocation is given a `DEFERRED` disposition, ADR-004's rejection clause a bucket-E carve-out, and Track C's exit a blocked register

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | P5-0, after DEV-128 and DEV-129 were drafted and still before any track started. Prompted by a contradiction pass over `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` against the live tree, asked for after two rounds of figure corrections. |
| **Original Plan** | `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` as corrected by DEV-129: Track A6 "Revoke the 602 scope-shaped A6 waivers"; Track E5 "Move the 347 A2 waiver entries out … into a plain backlog artifact that A16 reads"; Track A exit "`python -m audit` (full suite) and `python -m audit --only A16` both still exit cleanly"; Track C's per-batch loop gated on "exit 1 on any unwaived finding"; B7's ADR-004 amendment forbidding batch rejection of any row whose evidence line reads "no match"; C5 "one-time batch rejection of bucket E rows"; B3's bucket Z routing 80 rows to "record as blocked-by-decision, do not read"; Track C's exit "every tier-3 row is now tier 1 or tier 2"; A6's four-row split table of the 649 waivers; A7a "key off the reason prefix, so it revokes the 602 and leaves the 47 `A6 triage` entries standing". |
| **What Changed** | Five corrections, each verified against code or data. **(1) Revoking the waivers would have pinned the audit suite at exit 1 for the entire stage.** `AuditRun.exit_code` (`audit/__main__.py:104-105`) returns `1 if any(not f.waived …)`, and waivers are the only thing suppressing these findings — so A6's 602 plus E5's 347 = **949 findings that would report unwaived on every run** until Track C and Track D adjudicated all of them. That contradicts Track A's own exit criterion and the gate at the foot of every Track C batch, i.e. **no item in the checklist could have closed**. Fixed by making the move a **relocation with its own disposition**: E5 now creates `ingestion/audit/backlog.json`, A6 moves its 602 into the same file, and a finding matching a backlog entry is reported **`DEFERRED`** — excluded from `exit_code`, counted per check in the run summary. A waiver is a permanent judgement; a deferral is a queue position with a visible count that shrinks. Track A's exit now says **exit code 0** rather than "exit cleanly", which was the ambiguity hiding the conflict, and Track C's gate becomes "exit 0 **with a non-growing backlog**". E5 is a prerequisite for A6 as well as A7. **(2) B7's rejection clause forbade C5 outright.** Bucket E is *defined* as "neither name present", so every bucket-E row's evidence line reads "no match" by construction — the exact population B7 prohibits batch-rejecting. DEV-129 noticed the tension and resolved it by gating C5 on B2a, which is necessary but not sufficient: a clean alias layer changes bucket **D** membership, not whether a bucket-E row displays a matched span. Fixed with an explicit carve-out stated as a condition on the *segment*: where **neither** party is attested under any spelling either alias layer knows, **the absence is itself the displayed evidence** and the batch may reject; where **one** party is attested (bucket D), it may not, in either B2a state. B3's bucket D and bucket E dispositions and C5's scope are restated to match. The restatement also separates two routes that were being conflated: a bucket-E row in a passage Track C has **already opened** is decided per-row on that open segment like any other row — B7 constrains batch rejection *without* an opened segment, not review — so C5 narrows to the E rows in passages the queue never reached. Without that split, "E rows are only rejectable through C5" plus "C5 is optional" would have stranded them at tier 3 against the very exit criterion correction (3) was fixing. **(3) Track C's exit claimed an adjudication rate bucket Z excludes ~246 rows from.** "Every tier-3 row is now tier 1 or tier 2" cannot hold while bucket Z routes 80 D4-blocked rows to "record, do not read" and holds ~166 more for a Track D bound that reaches only 60 names. Fixed with the **bucket-Z blocked register**: rows that stay at tier 3 because a decision taken elsewhere in this stage makes them unseedable, each entry naming its blocker. Track C's exit, the stage-done criterion and F1 all now read "tier 1, tier 2, or in the register". The 108 junk-subject rows are explicitly *not* in it — a subject that can never become an entity is a decidable row, rejected at tier 2. **(4) A6's split table summed to 642, not 649, and named only 40 of the 47 keepers.** Measured: 602 `F0b`/`F0c` + 47 others, where the 47 break down **nine** ways — 15 / 15 / 7 / 3 as listed, plus `a NEW extraction-error shape` 2, `reversed direction` 2, `TRUE but reaches us under a…` 1, `GAP-007 / DEV-122:` 1, `DEV-122: … the CHILD is a…` 1. Table replaced with the two-way partition plus the nine-way breakdown and the construction that produced it. **(5) A7a's filter would have revoked 2 of the 47 verdicts it exists to protect.** Only **45** of the 47 carry the `A6 triage` prefix; the two `DEV-122` entries do not. A "keep iff starts with `A6 triage`" filter discards them — the same "discards real review work" failure A6 was rewritten to prevent, and the misfiling DEV-129 filed as a *future* risk while it was already live. Fixed by keying the filter off the **revoke** side (`reason.startswith(("F0b", "F0c"))`), with A7a's unit test asserting all 47 non-scope entries survive, the two `DEV-122` ones by name. |
| **Reason** | DEV-129 corrected the checklist's *figures*; these five are conflicts between two statements the checklist makes about its own execution, which arithmetic checking does not surface. Three of them (1, 2, 3) make a planned item unexecutable rather than merely misdescribed, and (1) would have been discovered only after A6 ran, at which point the suite would have been red with no item able to turn it green. All five were found by reading pairs of statements against each other and against `audit/__main__.py` and `audit-waivers.json`, not by re-deriving numbers. |
| **Impact** | **Documentation only — no code, no schema, no migration, no seeded-data change, no candidate-data change.** Files: `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` (A6, A7, A7a, Track A exit, B3 buckets D/E + Z, B7, Track C loop + exit + ceiling note, C5, E5, E6, Track E banner, Track order, F1, stage-done, deviation-protocol list — corrections inline and marked, superseded wording quoted where it was replaced), `docs/TODO2.md` (Stage P5 pointer refigured; the seeding rule's batch-closing clause now names the `DEFERRED` disposition), `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` (DEV-129 finding 3 annotated in place; this entry). No `.py`, `.kt`, `.sql` or `.json` file is touched — **including `audit-waivers.json`, which still holds all 1,095 entries.** **The re-scope and DEV-129's corrections both stand unchanged:** the passage axis, the 4,743-row / 715-group ceiling, the group-based headline, D1's 60-name bound and P5b's freeze are all untouched. |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Three of these are the same defect, and it is a boundary defect, not a carelessness defect.** Corrections (1), (2) and (3) each sit where a *rule* and a *task* written in the same document meet: the seeding rule's green-suite gate against A6's revocation; ADR-004's evidence clause against C5's sweep; Track C's exit against B3's bucket Z. Each half is correct read alone. DEV-129 already recorded this shape once — "A7's crash and E1's 'A1–A15 is enough' both come from writing a rule and a task in the same document without executing either" — and named the missing step as "checking that a planned item runs". That check catches (1), because a dry read of `exit_code` answers it in a minute. It does not catch (2) or (3), which are two rules disagreeing about the same rows with no code to run. The durable lesson is narrower and more useful than "verify the numbers": **every rule this stage adds needs one named item it forbids, and every exit criterion needs one named population it excludes.** Both are now written down where the rule is, not inferred later.

**The `DEFERRED` disposition is a real mechanism, not a rename.** It would be fair to ask whether moving 949 waivers into a file that suppresses the same findings is anything more than a relabelling. It is, in exactly one respect that matters: a waiver's count is not interesting and nothing watches it, while the deferral count is printed per check every run and Track C's batch gate requires it to be **non-growing**, and strictly lower for the checks a batch touched. The 602 A6 entries stop being invisible and become the stage's own progress bar. That is the difference DEV-128 was reaching for when it wrote "that is a backlog, not a waiver" — it just had no mechanism attached, and deletion was the only thing the sentence implied.

**Findings this pass did not fix:**

1. **The checklist's item labels A1–A9 collide with the audit checks named A1–A16.** Item A1 specifies a module whose `NAME` is `A16` and calls it a "sibling of `prominence.py` (A8)" while item A8 is about A3's cycles; item A7 is a waiver-filter task while D3 cites "`name_coverage.py`'s (A7) existing machinery"; item A9 concerns `<UNKNOWN>` in checks A8 and A2 while check A9 is `claim_type_distribution.py` and goes unmentioned. Item A2's body cites "the A2 four-way drop split" — the check, inside the item of the same name. Nothing is *wrong*, but the Track order block reads `A6, A7/A7a, A1-A3, A2a, A8` and a reader cannot tell tasks from checks without re-reading each item. Renumbering Track A (`A-1 …`, or `I1 …` for "instrument") is the fix and is not taken here because it would touch every cross-reference in the file and in DEV-128/129.
2. **The item count is stated three ways and all three are wrong.** The seeding rule's scope clause says "~22 of this stage's ~35 items", DEV-128 says "~35 items", `TODO2.md` says "~40". Measured: **43** items — A 13, B 9, C 6, D 4, E 7, F 4 — so non-seeding is **33 of 43**, not 22 of 35. The `~35` figures predate DEV-129 adding A2a, A9, A7a and B2a. This is the hand-quoted-count failure mode Track E3 exists to stop, reintroduced in the commit that wrote the rule; left standing because the clause's *argument* (most items add no rows) survives the correction unchanged.
3. **A16's headline group metric divides by the pool the seeding rule bans.** The rule says "coverage is always quoted against the reachable ceiling, never the raw candidate pool", the row secondary correctly uses 4,743, but the headline is `62/764` where 764 is the candidate-group pool and **715** is its reachable ceiling (`62/715 = 8.7%`). A2a's item text also specifies only the *row* ceiling derivation while Track C cites it for "the 4,743-row / **715-group** figure". Both are one-line fixes in A2/A2a and are deferred rather than taken, because changing the headline denominator before A16 exists risks the baseline being committed against a definition that then moves.
4. **A3 has A16 append `coverage_history.json` from `run()`,** while A1 and A3 both assert A16 "writes a report, not a tracker". An appended, committed history file *is* accumulated state written from `run()` — A16 would become the second such check after A10, in the stage that cites DEV-127's failed-open guard as the precedent to respect, and appending is worse than overwriting for that failure mode. Writing history only from a `main()`/`--out` path would match every other module in the package.
5. **DEV-129 describes DEV-128 as "committed" and "annotated in place"** while both entries land in the same uncommitted change (`git diff` at the time of this pass: `@@ -1673,3 +1673,57 @@`, 57 insertions, 0 deletions, HEAD `65a9bb7` holding neither). The quoted "as first written it read…" passages therefore describe a state that was never in git history, which is the one thing the append-only convention exists to make reconstructible. Committing DEV-128 before DEV-129 would have cost nothing; this entry inherits the same property and does not fix it.

## Docs infrastructure — DEVIATIONS.md archive + index (2026-07-30)

### DEV-131 — `DEVIATIONS.md` split into a generated index + per-phase archives; entries capped at ~4 KB

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | Docs infrastructure, between P5-0's planning and its Track A. Prompted by the file becoming unreadable in one pass. |
| **Original Plan** | `CLAUDE.md §Deviation Tracking Protocol` step 6: "Before starting any stage, re-read `DEVIATIONS.md`" — one append-only file, read whole. |
| **What Changed** | **(1)** DEV-001…DEV-057 (Phase 1) moved **verbatim** to `docs/deviations/phase1.md`; that file is closed. **(2)** `DEVIATIONS.md` gains a generated **Index** of all 126 entries, grouped by their original section headings, and keeps DEV-058 onward in full. **(3)** `scripts/deviations-index.py` regenerates the index (`--check` verifies it); the block is marked `INDEX:BEGIN/END` and never hand-edited. **(4)** Protocol step 6 now says read the *index*, plus new steps 7 (never hand-edit it; the counter is global and never forks) and 8 (**~4 KB per entry**, also added to `TODO2.md`'s cross-cutting rules and P5-0 Track E3). |
| **Reason** | The file reached **682 KB ≈ 169K tokens**, so the protocol step mandating a re-read before every stage could no longer be followed. Splitting *by topic* (the first proposal) was rejected on measurement: **58 of 125 entries (46%) touch both code and data**, so the axis has no clean cut and would need a hand-maintained classification — the failure mode DEV-129 finding 3 and DEV-130 correction (5) had just been fixed twice. Splitting by phase is lossless and needs no judgement. |
| **Impact** | **Documentation + one script; no code, schema, migration or data change.** Files: `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` (index + Phase 2), `docs/deviations/phase1.md` (new), `scripts/deviations-index.py` (new), `CLAUDE.md` (protocol steps 6–8), `docs/TODO2.md`, `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` (E3). **Verified: entry bodies are byte-identical** across the split (126 in, 126 out, one trailing section separator moved), **all 126 index anchors resolve**, and **every DEV id referenced anywhere in the repo still resolves** — so none of the ~340 inline `[DEVIATED - see DEVIATIONS.md #DEV-NNN]` markers needed rewriting. That was the property the design had to preserve. |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**The archive buys 29%; the size cap is the actual fix.** Phase 1 is only 194 KB of the 682 KB, because the file is not long in *entries* — it is long in *prose per entry*: the average grew **1.2 KB → 10.4 KB (8.5×)** from DEV-001…011 to DEV-126…130. At that rate the archive's headroom is gone in roughly one stage, which is why step 8's ~4 KB cap matters more than the split. DEV-130, written the same day, is 12 KB and the 4th-largest entry in the file; this entry is the first written under the cap.

**Findings this pass did not fix:**

1. **Nothing enforces the 4 KB cap or runs `--check`.** Both are conventions in `CLAUDE.md`. The repo has no docs CI, and adding one is out of scope here; until then a stale index or an oversized entry is caught only by review.
2. **Five ids were never written** — DEV-016/017 (reserved by ADR-009/ADR-010), DEV-106 (deliberately unclaimed), DEV-111 (folded into DEV-110). The index now lists them so a gap reads as deliberate, and the generator fails loudly if the gap set changes, but the underlying practice of reserving ids ahead of writing them is unchanged.
3. **DEV-015 sits out of id order**, under the ADR-008 section where it was written. Preserved rather than corrected: the section grouping is the real chronology and the file is append-only.

### DEV-132 — Five spec-shaped inconsistencies in the Stage P5 checklist fixed before Track A builds what they specify

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | P5-0, before any track started. Third correction pass, after DEV-129 (figures) and DEV-130 (execution-blocking conflicts); these are the medium/low findings of the same contradiction pass, triaged by whether unwritten code implements them. |
| **Original Plan** | `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` as corrected by DEV-130: the scope clause placing Tracks A/B/E/F wholly "not in scope"; A2's headline `62/764`; A2a specifying only the row ceiling; A3 appending `coverage_history.json` alongside "A16 writes a report, not a tracker"; DEV-129's `+43 entities`. |
| **What Changed** | **(1) Scope split in two.** The **batch-closing** requirement binds seeding batches only; the **detector budget binds every track**, since bounding row-free work is its whole purpose. The blanket "Tracks A/B/E/F not in scope" made A16's exemption redundant *and* left A9's legality undecided. **(2) A9 granted as a one-off budgeted bugfix**, explicitly rather than by implication — it corrects checks A2/A8 at 0 net rows, which the budget would otherwise forbid, deadlocking the stage a second way. Neither exemption is renewable. **(3) A2's headline divides by 715, not 764** — the reachable group ceiling — per the stage's own "always against the reachable ceiling" rule, which this row broke while the row secondary below it obeyed. The pool prints beside it, so the target reads as 715/715. **(4) A2a must report the group ceiling too** (715 of 764); three other places already cited it for both. **(5) `coverage_history.json` moves out of `run()`** to a `main()`/`--out` path: a report is reproducible, an appended history is accumulated committed state — the A10 shape DEV-127 caught failing open. **(6) `+43` → `+44` entities** (`0.87 × 2,337 = 2,033.2`; +43 gives 86.99%). |
| **Reason** | All five specify code that does not exist yet — A1–A3 implement the metric definitions and write paths, D1's bound rests on the entity arithmetic. A spec is free to fix before the code is written and costs a rewrite plus a DEV entry afterwards. DEV-130 deferred (3) and (4) reasoning that changing the denominator "before A16 exists risks the baseline being committed against a definition that then moves". That was backwards: A16 does not exist, so there is no baseline to move. |
| **Impact** | **Documentation only — no code, schema, migration or data change.** Files: `docs/TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md` (scope + exemptions, A2, A2a, A3, Track D preamble), `docs/TODO2.md` (mirrored seeding rule), `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` (DEV-129's `+43` annotated in place; this entry). **The stage's structure, ceilings, bound and freeze are unchanged** — every fix sharpens a definition rather than moving a target. |
| **Date** | 2026-07-30 |

**Findings this pass did not fix** — the four judged prose rather than spec, deferred deliberately so they are not lost:

1. **Checklist item labels `A1–A9` collide with the audit checks `A1–A16`.** Item A1 specifies a module named `A16` and calls it "sibling of `prominence.py` (A8)" while item A8 concerns A3's cycles; D3 cites "`name_coverage.py`'s (A7)" while item A7 is the waiver filter. Renumbering would touch every cross-reference here and in DEV-128/129/130; the cheap fix is a **convention at the ~12 ambiguous sites** — "check A8 (`prominence.py`)" vs bare `A8`.
2. **One stale item count survives**: the seeding rule now reads 33 of 43 (measured), but DEV-128's Impact still says "~35 items". Left as the record of what that commit claimed.
3. **"Even adding all 20 … reaches only 53.7%"** overstates — 53.7% clears the ≥53% edge exit. The conclusion survives (the achievable 13 names give 50.6%), but D1's rejection of the 45-name bound still omits its stronger reason: 45 misses the edge exit outright at 52.6%.
4. **DEV-129 calls DEV-128 "committed" and "annotated in place"** while both landed in one uncommitted change, so the superseded wording it quotes was never in git history. Unfixable after the fact.

### DEV-136 — Track C1 batch 1 (`hesiod-theogony 346-403`): 31 promoted, 18 rejected, 7 of 9 rejected groups share one collision shape

| **Stage** | P5-0 Track C, sprint C1, first passage off the B4 queue (top of the queue by contested-row count). |
| **Original Plan** | Track C's per-batch loop applied to one passage; developer-reviewed per ADR-004 Amendment 1. |
| **What Changed** | 55 tier-3 rows read against the cited segment and cross-checked against live `entities`/`relationships`/`entity_aliases`. 31 promoted, 18 rejected, 6 left tier-3 (Z-bucket). Keys in `promotion_log.json` batch `p5-track-c1-batch1-hesiod-theogony-346-403`. |
| **Reason** | 4 rejected rows contradict the passage's own text (`Zeus \| child of Styx/Pallas` — the passage names their children as Zelus/Nike/Kratos/Bia; `Perses \| child of Oceanus/Tethys` — the same passage gives Perses' real parents as Eurybia/Crius). 14 rejected rows are one recurring shape: a minor Oceanid catalogue name resolved onto an unrelated, already-seeded entity sharing that name — confirmed against the DB before rejecting, not guessed. `Pluto`→Hades (`entity_aliases`: Pluto/Dis→Hades); `Urania`→the Muse (Zeus+Mnemosyne, 2 sources); `Rhode`(`Rhodea`)→Poseidon+Amphitrite's daughter; `Chryses`(`Chryseis`)→Minos's son; `Europa`→Agenor's daughter; `Polydora`→Peleus's daughter. `Ianira`(`Ianeira`)→Nereus's daughter is the one genuinely ambiguous pair (Hesiod plausibly reuses the name across his own Oceanid and Nereid catalogues) — rejected conservatively rather than asserted. |
| **Impact** | `seedgen --strict` regenerated V12 locally (300→331 rows); reseed/audit against the live DB not yet run (blocked on a running `core-api` on :8080). 7 of 9 rejected groups sharing one collision shape in a single passage suggests it recurs — a candidate for a `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` line and eventually a systematic check, not built now (would spend Track A's detector budget on one passage's evidence). |
| **Date** | 2026-07-31 |
