### DEV-138 — Track C1 batch 3 (5 passages, parallel subagent review): 174 promoted, 78 rejected — collision shape now confirmed already-live in three seeded/promoted rows

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | P5-0 Track C1, passages 3–7 off the B4 queue, reviewed by 5 parallel subagents (one passage each, same methodology and worked examples from DEV-136/137 as calibration), merged by the lead session after validating no cross-passage key conflicts. Per user instruction, `seedgen`/`reseed`/live audit **not** run this batch — candidate-file writes only. |
| **Original Plan** | Track C's per-batch loop, one passage per subagent, developer-reviewed per ADR-004 Amendment 1. |
| **What Changed** | 277 tier-3 rows across `hesiod-theogony 233-269` (75), `apollodorus-bibliotheca 2.1.5` (40), `1.2.1-1.2.7` (102), `2.4.5` (21), `3.10.8-3.11.1` (39). Totals: **174 promoted, 78 rejected, 25 left tier-3** (Z-bucket). Per-passage keys in `promotion_log.json` batches `p5-track-c1-batch3-<source>-<ref>`. |
| **Reason** | Same collision shape as DEV-136/137, confirmed at scale: **≥60 of 78** rejections are a name in the passage resolving onto an unrelated, already-established DB entity — new instances include the Muse Erato (2 passages), Theban royals Agave/Autonoe (2 passages, both also colliding with Hesiod's own Nereid catalogue), the Argonaut Idas, King Oeneus of Calydon, and a severe case in `2.4.5` where the passage's own "Amphitryon" (Heracles' stepfather) was resolved throughout to the unrelated **Amphictyon** (legendary Athenian king) — 7 of that passage's 17 rejections alone. `2.1.5` was the extreme case: 31 of 40 rows rejected, nearly every Danaid-catalogue name colliding with a famous unrelated namesake. |
| **Impact** | **Three separate instances where this collision had already reached already-live data**, beyond the candidate pool this review covers: (1) `relationships` already has `Cronus parent_of Leonteus` (should be a mortal "Coronus", `3.10.8-3.11.1`); (2) `relationships` already conflates Amphitryon and Amphictyon across several rows for `2.4.5`/`2.4.6`/`2.4.7-2.4.8`/`1.8.2`; (3) the `Lynceus` entity carrying `2.1.5`'s own central Hypermnestra/Abas plot thread is already resolved to the wrong Lynceus (Aphareus's son) — and in `2.4.5` a **promoted** (`trust_tier=1`) `variant_claims` row already conflates Perses/Perseus on the same entity. None fixed by this entry — flagged for a dedicated look, since `relationships` has no human gate and a promoted row needs its own review, not a Track C candidate decision. Separately: `Agave`/`Autonoe` carry `subtype='nereid'` in `entities` itself while also being established Theban royalty — the collision is baked into the entity record from original extraction, not just candidate review, closer to GAP-006's shape than a fixable `trust_tier` call. Five passages now show this pattern consistently enough (≥60/78 this batch, 22/30 across DEV-136/137) that a systematic check may be worth its own decision, not built here. |

### DEV-139 — GAP-009 + GAP-010 rescoped into a new Stage P6 (ADR-022), interrupting P5 Track C before C2

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Stage** | P5-0 Track C1, after batch 3 (7 passages adjudicated; batches `p5-track-c1-batch1..3-*` in `promotion_log.json`). Planning only — no code, no seeding, no live runs in this pass. |
| **Original Plan** | GAP-009 and GAP-010 were filed 2026-07-31 as two separate open gaps homed to "P5 (extraction-quality)", each with an unanswered "what a fix needs to decide" section. DEV-138 recorded that "a systematic check may be worth its own decision, not built here." |
| **What Changed** | One root cause identified for both, and the decision taken: **ADR-022** (`adr-022-entity-identity-and-namesake-resolution.md`, Proposed) + **Stage P6** (`TODO-phase2-stage-p6.md`, 8 tracks G0–G7), inserted **inside P5 Track C1 — after batch 3, before batch 4**, not at the C1/C2 boundary (C1's remaining ~93 passages grow the exposure exactly as C2's would). `TODO2.md` gains the P6 stage entry and a C-track interrupt banner; `TODO-phase2-stage-p5.md`'s *Track order* and **C1** item carry the gate; both GAP entries move to "owned by Stage P6" with their rows-at-stake lines and their decided-questions sections. |
| **Reason** | Both gaps are one defect: **entity identity is decided by string matching, silently, with no evidence artifact and no review gate.** `EntityResolver.resolve()` matches exact → `known_aliases.json` → rapidfuzz@88; it does not know the passage a name came from and has no access to the confirmed entity set. `relationships` inherits that with no human gate; `variant_claims` inherits it through a gate that reviews *what the claim says* and takes *who the subject is* as given. Threshold tuning is ruled out on measurement — construction `rapidfuzz.fuzz.ratio(a,b)`: every confirmed false positive scores **88.9–92.3**, every legitimate spelling variant DEV-043 cared about scores **83.3**, i.e. already below the cutoff and handled by the curated alias layers. The full table is in ADR-022 *Context* and in GAP-009's item 1. |
| **Impact** | **Sequencing is the substantive part.** `build_candidates` re-resolves from *cached* segment facts, so a resolver change costs **zero API calls** — but it rewrites `subject_name`, part of `_CLAIM_IDENTITY`, so `_write_claims_preserving_review` drops the affected verdicts through its "no longer produced" path. Exposure, construction `Counter(r.get('trust_tier',3) for r in variant_claims_candidates.json)`: **569 tier-1 + 523 tier-2 = 1,092 decisions** of 7,429 rows, growing with every batch — hence G0 (key migration) first and the stage before the *next batch* rather than after Track C. **Detector budget: zero spent** — all new tooling lives in `extraction/`, outside the `audit` package that `discover_checks()` walks, so it is never enumerated (location, not the absent `NAME`; the Track B1 argument), and **A1** (threshold-88 pass *plus* its transliteration pass, which is what covers the sub-88 variants) is the recall guard for G2's fuzzy decision, so E1's "A16 is the last check" holds. Under the findings rule the **five** already-live defects are **class 1** (the only class that interrupts) — enumerated once in `TODO-phase2-stage-p6.md` → *The class-1 set*, which supersedes DEV-138's differently-scoped count of three; the rest is **class 4** with its row-yield hypothesis stated in G5 and explicitly *not* linearly extrapolated from 7 catalogue-heavy passages. Two mechanism corrections carried into the plan: the registry is consulted **first, ahead of the exact-match memo** (a lookup merely "before the alias step" sits behind `_seen`'s exact hit and never fires for GAP-010), and `_seen` is re-keyed per passage (G3.2a) or the registry's answer leaks to every later passage. Known limit accepted in ADR-022: a `(name, source_id, passage_ref)` key cannot split two figures sharing one passage (`Lynceus` @ `2.1.5`), fixed by hand in G4.4. |
| **Date** | 2026-07-31 |
